target_customer: Teams who wanted to reduce internal email with threaded, presence aware chat
problem: Work conversation was stuck in email. Hum was a chat program that integrated with email, organized conversation into threads with presence, and let users send work requests to each other's feeds.
business_model: Team collaboration software; monetization not stated in sources opened

founders.name: Dann Petty
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background given. A Dribbble profile with the same name shows a San Francisco designer but does not mention Hum, so it was not used.

competitors.name: Yammer
competitors.what: Enterprise social network owned by Microsoft
competitors.traction_then: Named on Hum's YC S13 directory page as a major incumbent

competitors.name: Asana
competitors.what: Work management and task collaboration tool
competitors.traction_then: Named on Hum's YC S13 directory page

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time threaded chat with presence, email integration and cross device sync is standard but non trivial for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Team chat was commoditizing quickly; no data or network lock in is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented. Slack publicly launched in August 2014 and took the category, but no source ties it to Hum's fate.

market_need_then: The YC page frames Hum as disrupting email with collaboration, but gives no demand evidence, customers or usage figures.

brand_strength.rationale: A short real word name but no press, brand assets or community found; later unrelated companies use the same name.

outcome_analysis: Hum joined YC in Summer 2013 as a chat product integrated with email, with a team of 11 listed on the YC page. Directories mark it inactive or dead, but no launch press, funding record, shutdown announcement or cause was found, so the cause of failure is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: No company website is listed on the YC page and none was found. Funding searches returned only unrelated companies named Hum (Hum Capital, Hum Systems) so no rounds are recorded. The competitor entries come from the YC directory description, which is undated, so source_date is given only as 2013; no dated third party coverage was found.
